## Trial `traffic-shaping-centos-stream10__YuyjXHj`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All three material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct measurement evidence: the private node2<->node1<->node3 path was correctly identified and addressed, node2->node3 traffic was capped to ~1 Mbit/s via a node2-side HTB/u32 tc configuration (persisted via systemd and reverified after a reboot), and node3->node2 traffic remained unrestricted (~1-19 Gbit/s) both before and after restarts. The provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all three nodes with clear pre-restart boot identity, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered network/shaping state, cross-checked successfully against the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshots. The main deduction is operational hygiene: iperf3 test tooling and firewalld port openings used for verification were not cleaned up afterward, leaving minor unnecessary residue and an open (unused) port on node2 and node3.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.650 | 0.900 | 58/7 (+10 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1-topology-routing — Satisfied:** Establish/confirm the real private routed path node2 <-> node1 <-> node3 (addressing and routes) needed to apply directional shaping
  - **Why:** Executor discovered node1 eth1/eth2 and node2/node3 enp8s0 as the unaddressed private links (distinct from shared mgmt network), assigned 10.50.1.0/24 and 10.50.2.0/24, added static routes via nmcli on node2/node3 and VyOS config on node1, and verified end-to-end connectivity (ping and iperf3 both directions) both before and after all three nodes were rebooted.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-a2d3c159d7554dd1`, `cmd-f10b23ce33a34d69`, `cmd-1922fda457854d00`, `cmd-6dec5dabda544a7f`, `cmd-ef20f619b34d4ae0`, `cmd-dff9e1ca8a6b4aa3`, `cmd-3ffaef31e7f14530`, `cmd-d0450984fb9245b0`, `cmd-0608a3bc14e74d4e`, `cmd-9791ff6ab3e34727`, `cmd-327e8f998de0408d`, `cmd-663ab618a6d14368`, `cmd-6fe4ec33f93c4dbf`
- **req-2-shape-node2-to-node3 — Satisfied:** Limit traffic from node2 toward node3 to 1 Mbit/s
  - **Why:** An HTB qdisc with u32 filter matching dst 10.50.2.0/24 was applied on node2's enp8s0 (the node3-facing interface), classifying that traffic into a 1mbit-capped class. Baseline unshaped throughput was ~18.7 Gbit/s; after shaping, UDP iperf3 node2->node3 measured sender 1.05 Mbit/s / receiver 973 Kbit/s, directly at the 1 Mbit/s target. Shaping was persisted via a systemd unit and re-verified functioning after a full node2 reboot, with post-reboot throughput ~1.13/0.96 Mbit/s.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-0ee2344b7b0e4648`, `cmd-ce806a3325354b70`, `cmd-365cf74533b549a6`, `cmd-2c7c35dd196941d8`, `cmd-663ab618a6d14368`, `cmd-7be5071e1c6f4c0b`
- **req-3-unrestricted-node3-to-node2 — Satisfied:** Leave traffic from node3 toward node2 unrestricted
  - **Why:** No shaping was applied on node3, and the node2 HTB filter only matches traffic destined for 10.50.2.0/24, leaving the default class (1:30, 10gbit) for other traffic including the return path. iperf3 measured node3->node2 throughput at ~1.07 Gbit/s immediately after shaping was applied and ~1.21 Gbit/s after node3 was rebooted, confirming the reverse direction remained unrestricted both before and after shaping/restart.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-2b668176501d49c7`, `cmd-3e0a426ab6a34163`, `cmd-002c7099844f48c0`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.650**. Core actions (topology discovery, IP/route configuration, tc HTB shaping, systemd persistence unit) were purposeful and directly tied to the task or to bounded verification. However, several testing-support mutations were left in place rather than cleaned up: firewalld ports 5201/tcp and 5201/udp were opened on node2 (cmd-2ef31826e77a4b90, cmd-f764bff3d8914c81) and node3 (cmd-1d30929542924bad, cmd-16792a45dc344382, cmd-dccfda45052e4260) for iperf3 testing and were never closed, leaving an unnecessary open port on both hosts after the iperf3 server processes were killed (cmd-c233c87718924a2e, cmd-1acdca96dfac4fae). Iperf3 packages (cmd-b9598b8f10d34b48, cmd-85cc0d12b95745ce) and associated log/pid files under /tmp also remained as residue on node2/node3 per the after_executor snapshot. These are low-risk, bounded artifacts (no failed services, no package-manager corruption, no unrelated config drift), but the unclosed firewall ports represent a minor weakened security posture that was not reverted.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-1d30929542924bad`, `cmd-2ef31826e77a4b90`, `cmd-16792a45dc344382`, `cmd-dccfda45052e4260`, `cmd-f764bff3d8914c81`, `cmd-c233c87718924a2e`, `cmd-1acdca96dfac4fae`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- TCP throughput test immediately after applying shaping (cmd-e953e5b375e848cf) showed throughput dropping to 0 mid-test; this appears to be an artifact of TCP behavior over a severely constrained link with sfq, not a failure of the cap itself, but it was not further explained.
- Restart evidence, while thorough, is independent of the public task contract (no reboot/persistence requirement was stated); it is treated here as supplemental confidence-building evidence, not as a scored task requirement.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.650); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.900; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
